samples.summary: The slides clipboard is a second attacker-reachable entry for the same Block model and bypasses the new sanitizer entirely
samples.evidence: The diff hardens `deserializeBlocks`/`deserializeClipboard` because "the `WAFFLEDOCS_MIME` flavour is JSON that *any* page can put on the system clipboard" and an unvalidated cast lets a hostile page write arbitrary values "straight into the shared Yorkie tree, the renderer, and the DOCX/PDF exporters". The parallel slides path does exactly the old thing: `packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/clipboard.ts:48` — `return parsed.elements;` after only `magic === MAGIC` + `Array.isArray(elements)` (`isPayload`, line 51-58). It is reachable from the system clipboard: `packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:816-819` reads `MIME_TYPE` off `navigator.clipboard` and hands the blob to `deserializeElements`, and line 847 does the same for the event path; the function is also re-exported publicly as `SLIDES_CLIPBOARD_MIME`/`deserializeElements` from `packages/slides/src/index.ts:228`. Slides text elements carry docs `Block[]` (same `type`/`headingLevel`/`tableData`/`inlines` shape — `packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts` imports `Block`, `HeadingLevel` from `@wafflebase/docs`), which reach the docs layout engine, the shared Yorkie tree and the exporters. Fix belongs on the slides clipboard (reuse the new sanitizer, or an element-level equivalent), not on the diff.

samples.summary: The two new headingLevel removals use the subtree-spanning `removeStyleByPath(path, path+1)` pattern the same file documents as wrong and provides `removeNodeStyle` to avoid
samples.evidence: `removeNodeStyle` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:275) exists precisely because "`removeStyleByPath(path, path+1, …)` looks node-scoped but is not: that path range spans the node's whole subtree, and Yorkie applies the removal to every element node in it" (comment at 260-274). `setBlockType` honours that helper for exactly this attribute at line 1466 (`removeNodeStyle(tree, blockPath, toRemove)` where `toRemove` may contain `headingLevel`). The new split path (line 2064-2068) and merge path (line 2250-2253) instead hand-roll `endPath = blockPath+1` and call `tree.removeStyleByPath(blockPath, endPath, ['headingLevel'])`, re-introducing the subtree-wide removal the helper was written to prevent. Today the only descendants of a text block are inline nodes, which never carry `headingLevel`, so the blast radius is latent rather than observable — but the two writers of the same attribute now disagree on scoping, and nothing in CI covers the distinction. Fix belongs on the new code (call `removeNodeStyle`).

samples.summary: The content PUT API writes `headingLevel` and block `type` with no validation — the second untrusted entry the clipboard sanitizer's threat model names, left unguarded
samples.evidence: The new sanitizer's rationale (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:36-45) is that an unchecked `headingLevel`/unknown `type` must not reach "the shared Yorkie tree, the renderer, and the DOCX/PDF exporters", and the diff's own test asserts a `headingLevel` of `'1" w:customStyle="1'` is dropped. `assertValidBlock` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:365-379) validates only `id`, `type` as `typeof === 'string'` (no allowlist), and `style`; it never inspects `headingLevel`, `listKind`, `listLevel` or `marker`, and the controller comment at 137-140 says as much ("We validate just the fields the writer unconditionally dereferences"). The value then reaches `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:241-242` as `attrs.headingLevel = String(block.headingLevel)` for any block type, and `packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:128` already documents that `headingLevel` "reaches this exporter as whatever was persisted (import, the content PUT API)". Impact is bounded because `toHeadingStyleId` (docx-style-map.ts:139) and `blockStyleId` (named-styles.ts:108) clamp at their sinks, so this is the defence-in-depth gap rather than an exploitable escape.

samples.summary: `mergeDropsHeadingMemory`/`splitMovesHeadingMemory` decide from the cached block's inlines inside the two functions that document the cache's inlines can diverge from the tree
samples.evidence: Both new predicates key on `block.inlines` text length (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:295-322). In `YorkieDocStore.mergeBlock` the input is the cache (`firstBlock = this.getBlockByRegion(...)`, line 2222) and the very next comment in the same `doc.update` says: "Read inline count from the actual tree, not the cache, because previous split/merge operations can leave the tree with a different number of inline nodes than the cache (e.g. split fragments)" (line 2255-2257). `splitBlock` reads the same cached block at line 2041 and even branches on `hasInlineChildren` read from the *tree* at 2073. So the has-no-text-of-its-own decision that drives a CRDT attribute write is taken from a source the surrounding code explicitly distrusts; when the two disagree the remembered level is dropped/moved against the text actually in the tree. Cache and tree stay mutually consistent (one predicate drives both), so the impact is a wrong-but-consistent heading memory rather than divergence between peers.

samples.summary: No persistence format outside the Yorkie tree carries the new list-item heading memory, so it silently dies on any export/import or PPTX round trip
samples.evidence: The new invariant is that a `list-item` keeps `headingLevel` so un-listing restores the heading. Every serializer gates on `type === 'heading'` and therefore drops it: `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:207` (`block.type === 'heading' ? block.headingLevel : undefined`), `packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts:103-115` (the `list-item` arm emits only the marker), and the slides side never reads it at all (Grep for `headingLevel` in packages/slides/src returns only the `getBlockType`/`setBlockType` API signatures, so `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts` cannot round-trip it). The diff's own tests assert this inertness for markdown/DOCX, so the loss is intentional for export — but it means a docs → DOCX → docs or slides → PPTX → slides trip converts every bulleted heading into a plain bullet, which is the exact downgrade #783 was filed about. Worth a deliberate decision rather than an accident.
searchedFor: Grep 'headingLevel' across packages/docs/src, packages/slides/src, packages/cli, packages/backend/src
read pdf-exporter.ts addOutlineFromHeadings, markdown.ts blockToMarkdown, named-styles.ts blockStyleId

verdict.reason: Verified independently: packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/clipboard.ts:38-58 parses clipboard JSON, checks only the magic string and Array.isArray, and returns parsed.elements as Element[] with no field validation. It is reachable from the system clipboard at keyboard.ts:819 (custom MIME), :827 and :847 (text/plain fallback via tryDeserialize), and the Cmd+V handler (keyboard.ts:343-361) hands the result to pasteElements (paste.ts:40-92), which only spreads/casts to ElementInit; SlidesMemoryStore.addElement (store/memory.ts:558-593) clones and reassigns the id, validating nothing (only connector frame recompute). The only filter on the path is the board table-type gate at keyboard.ts:353-355. Slides text elements do carry docs Block[] (model/element.ts:1 and :265) which feed the docs-derived renderer/layout/autofit and the PPTX exporter. I searched packages/slides/src for sanitize|normalizeElement|validateElement|isElement|assertElement (zero hits) and enumerated every deserializeElements caller repo-wide; the docs sanitizer (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:45-353) is wired only into deserializeBlocks/deserializeClipboard and is not reached from any slides path. No counterexample exists, so the reviewer's absence claim holds, and it is in the blast-radius lane: a parallel attacker-reachable entry point into the same model consumers that bypasses the new validation.

finding.summary: `insertPlainText` still hits the `Doc.splitBlock` empty-list-item short-circuit that `insertBlocks` was just patched to avoid — and the diff makes that short-circuit convert the block to a heading
finding.evidence: The diff adds a workaround in `insertBlocks` (text-editor.ts:3610-3626) because `Doc.splitBlock` returns the *same* block id for an empty list item instead of splitting (document.ts:303-307). The sibling caller `insertPlainText` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3536) was not updated: with the caret in an empty bullet, `docSplitBlock` returns the same id, the cursor is moved to offset 0 of that same block, and every subsequent line is prepended into one block — multi-line plain-text paste (Ctrl+Shift+V / `pastePlainTextFromClipboard`, text-editor.ts:3498-3510) collapses and reverses the lines. This change additionally makes that short-circuit convert an empty *bulleted heading* into a `heading` block (document.ts:301-307), so the same paste now also silently promotes the destination to Heading N. `ensureEditableBlock` (line 3520) is unaffected (hr/page-break only) and `editor.ts:3258/3277` are guarded by `offset > 0 && offset < len`.

verdict.reason: The described code is present as claimed. Doc.splitBlock short-circuits on an empty list-item, returning the same blockId and converting the block through unlistedBlockType (so a remembered headingLevel promotes it to a `heading`) at packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:297-307 / types.ts:337-344. insertBlocks was given an explicit workaround for that short-circuit (text-editor.ts:3613-3631), but the sibling caller insertPlainText calls docSplitBlock at text-editor.ts:3540-3544 and then moves the cursor to offset 0 of the returned id, assuming a new tail block always exists; docSplitBlock (text-editor.ts:407-411) adds no guard and ensureEditableBlock (3520-3527) only covers horizontal-rule/page-break. The path is reachable via Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V (text-editor.ts:1058-1061 -> 3502-3514) and the plain-text paste fallback (text-editor.ts:1194-1196). Whenever a split target is an empty list item (leading blank line, or any blank line inside the pasted text, which leaves the freshly split empty list-item as the next split target), the next line folds back into the same block and the block is silently unlisted/promoted. The reviewer's symptom description is somewhat overstated (the fold does not repeat for every subsequent line), but the un-updated consumer of the changed splitBlock contract is real and squarely in the blast-radius lane; I cannot refute it on any named ground.

finding.summary: The slides clipboard reaches the same docs `Block` model with no validation, bypassing the new `deserializeBlocks` sanitizer's threat model
finding.evidence: The diff hardens the docs internal clipboard because "any page can put [it] on the system clipboard" and unvalidated values flow "straight into the shared Yorkie tree, the renderer, and the DOCX/PDF exporters" (clipboard.ts:34-43). `packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/clipboard.ts:38-49` parses a JSON payload, checks only a `magic` string, and returns `parsed.elements as Element[]`; `Element` carries `blocks: Block[]` of the identical docs model (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:1,265). It is reached from the paste handler at packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:819 and — worse — from `tryDeserialize` on the plain `text/plain` flavour at keyboard.ts:847, which any page can write. Those blocks are rendered by the shared docs text-box renderer and exported (PPTX/PDF), so the class of injection the diff closes for docs remains open one package over. Fix belongs on the slides deserializer (reuse a shared block sanitizer).

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. `deserializeElements` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/clipboard.ts:38-58) validates only the `magic` string and `Array.isArray(elements)`, then casts untrusted JSON to `Element[]`; `Element`/`TextBody.blocks` is the identical docs `Block[]` model imported from `@wafflebase/docs` (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:1,265). The path is reachable from the Cmd+V handler via the custom MIME (keyboard.ts:816-819) and, critically, via `tryDeserialize` on plain `text/plain` (keyboard.ts:823-827, 845-851), which any page's copy handler can write. Nothing downstream validates: paste.ts:51-70 spreads the payload into `ElementInit` and store/memory.ts:558-593 only clones and reassigns the id. I traced the complete path from clipboard read to store insert and grepped repo-wide for any sanitizer (`sanitiz|deserializeBlocks|validateBlock`, `normalizeElement|sanitizeElement|validateElement|coerceElement`); the only sanitizer in the repo is packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts (the diff itself), and the only slides match is a test helper (packages/slides/test/export/pptx/normalize.ts:125). Those blocks flow into shared docs layout/render code (e.g. packages/slides/src/model/autofit.ts:77 calls docs `computeLayout`) and are persisted to the collaborative store, so the exact class of injection the docs sanitizer closes (per its own comment at packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:36-43) remains reachable through the slides package, and `deserializeElements` is even re-exported publicly at packages/slides/src/index.ts:228 for the frontend wrapper. In-lane as a parallel entry point into the same shared model that never passes the sanitizing invariant; major impact (unvalidated attacker data into a shared, persisted model consumed by shared renderer/exporters).
